pick.headline: Police beat students in Prague, starting the Velvet Revolution
pick.summary: On November 17, 1989, riot police attacked a student march in Prague. The beating set off the mass protests that brought down Czechoslovakia's communist government within weeks.
pick.significance: The Velvet Revolution completed the collapse of communist rule in Central Europe in the autumn of 1989.
pick.fbis: Czechoslovak television's evening report of November 17, which FBIS headed 'Antisocialist' Forces Demonstrate, followed the students' procession for International Students Day as it happened.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: East Europe, No. 222, 20 November 1989
evidence.snippet: FBIS-EEU-89-222 20 November 1989 ‘Antisocialist’ Forces Demonstrate 17 Nov LD1711192589 Prague Television Service in Czech 1830 GMT 17 Nov 89 [Text] [Unidentified reporter] It is exactly 1600, and participants in this year’s students’ procession, which is taking place on the occasion of International Students Day…
